# cookiecutter-ai-saas

> cookiecutter-ai-saas is an open-source (MIT) cookiecutter template, maintained by CrimsonCow Labs, that generates a full-stack AI SaaS application: a Next.js 16 app in TypeScript with sign-in and optional Stripe billing, a Python worker that runs a bounded LangGraph agent, Postgres, Redis and BullMQ for background jobs, and a Docker Compose stack behind Caddy that Ansible provisions and deploys to a VPS. It is pre-release and not yet recommended for production use.

## What it includes

- App: Next.js 16, React 19 and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS and DaisyUI. Sign-in and dashboard pages, plus a settings page with plan and billing when Stripe is on.
- Auth: NextAuth v5 with Google and/or Microsoft OAuth, and optional email magic-link sign-in via Resend.
- Billing: optional Stripe checkout and customer portal.
- Worker: a Python worker that consumes BullMQ jobs and hands them to a bounded, tool-calling LangGraph agent, reporting progress as it goes.
- Data: PostgreSQL through Drizzle ORM, with optional pgvector for vector similarity search.
- Queue: Redis and BullMQ between the app and the worker.
- Deployment: Docker Compose behind Caddy (automatic TLS), with Ansible playbooks to provision a Debian-family VPS, deploy, and schedule database backups.

Choices made once, at generation time:

- LLM provider: Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter.
- Stripe billing: on or off (off leaves the checkout, customer portal, webhook and billing settings page out of the generated project).
- OAuth providers: Google and Microsoft, Google only, or Microsoft only.
- Magic-link sign-in via Resend: on or off.
- pgvector: on or off.
- Marketing extras (a JSON-backed blog and a contact form): on or off.
- Naming and defaults: project name, slug and description, author, domain, brand colour and theme, Python and Node.js versions, local Postgres and Redis ports.

## How to install

Prerequisites: Python and pip (for cookiecutter), Node.js (20 or newer by default), Docker with Docker Compose, and Poetry for running the Python worker locally (Python 3.14 by default). A production deployment also needs a Debian-family VPS (Ubuntu LTS) reachable over SSH, a domain name, and Ansible.

```bash
pip install cookiecutter
cookiecutter gh:CrimsonCowLabs/cookiecutter-ai-saas
cd <project-slug>
./setup.sh
```

`./setup.sh` checks for Node.js and Docker, writes the env files, generates a NEXTAUTH_SECRET, prompts for credentials for the optional features you kept, runs `npm ci`, starts the Docker Compose services, and generates and applies the database migrations.

## Status

Pre-release. The template generates and runs today and is being hardened ahead of its first tagged release; there is no tagged release yet, and it is not yet recommended for production use.
